title: deepDTnet repurposes topotecan as an RORγt inhibitor for multiple-sclerosis models
summary: The deep-learning network deepDTnet predicted retinoic-acid-receptor-related orphan receptor gamma-t (RORγt) as a previously unrecognized target of topotecan. Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.
ai_technology: deepDTnet, heterogeneous drug–gene–disease network embedding with deep learning
organization: Cleveland Clinic, Case Western Reserve University, Harvard Medical School and collaborators

evidence.tested: Biochemical assays showed direct inhibition (IC50 0.43 μM), and topotecan improved outcomes in a mouse experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis.
evidence.unknown: Evidence is preclinical: direct target and mouse-model assays do not establish safety or effectiveness in people with multiple sclerosis. Topotecan is an established anticancer drug, and its new target/indication remains a repurposing hypothesis.
evidence.ai_role: The model integrated 15 types of chemical, genomic, phenotypic and cellular network profiles to rank new drug targets. It nominated RORγt for topotecan, which the team tested using direct binding/transcriptional assays and a mouse EAE disease model.
